evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary records 嗎 as a colloquial variant of 罵, citing 字彙 (“俗罵字”) and earlier dictionary traditions. For the ‘scold’ reading it analyzes 口 as semantic and 馬 as phonetic; it also says 嗎 has a separate proper-character entry. This account concerns the ‘scold’ use, not the history of the question particle.
evidence.title: [A03210-003] 嗎 (罵) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The entry says 嗎 is not recorded in Shuowen and gives sentence-final interrogative and pause/topic-marking uses. It quotes a question from 董解元《西廂記》卷四 and another from 《老殘遊記》第三回, without dating the quoted passage. Its accessible form table lists later dictionary witnesses, but no continuous ancient graphic sequence.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org 嗎 Chinese character glyph historical 嗎
search_audit.outcome: Search results and inspected official rights notice confirmed Xiaoxuetang query-interface glyph outputs are CC0 1.0, but no actual 嗎 glyph asset and provenance page was found. No Commons candidate for 嗎 was established.

The four requested character-specific Unihan endpoints returned internal errors. General Unihan documentation and unrelated index resources were accessible but do not substitute for the individual records.

gaps: No primary paleographic sequence for 嗎 or 吗 was established. The Ministry of Education entry says 嗎 is absent from Shuowen and its accessible form table has no published ancient-form records; no corruption claim is supported.

The graphic analysis 口 (semantic) + 馬 (phonetic) is specifically supported for the older 嗎-as-罵 lexical use. Evidence examined does not establish that this component analysis explains the graph’s later question-particle use.

The question particle’s earliest surviving use and its semantic transition from negative existential 無 through forms such as 麼 remain outside this run’s inspected primary evidence. The literary quotation cited by the Ministry of Education is undated on that page.

Official Unihan character-specific endpoints failed in this run, and a current pronunciation comparison for 吗/嗎 versus 马/馬 could not be independently verified here. Historical pronunciation evidence from a component cannot be transferred to the host.

No usable glyph image candidate was located with verified identity, direct image URL, and provenance. Since the graphic history of 嗎 itself is undocumented in the inspected sources, no image is proposed.

limitations.text: No image candidate: the inspected primary entry reports no Shuowen form and exposes no ancient glyph records for 嗎; the Xiaoxuetang search did not yield a character-specific 嗎 record or image. Consequently there is no justified period-specific glyph candidate or direct image URL to select.
